findings.title: The bert-base-cased alias resolves equivalently to the canonical google-bert checkpoint ID
findings.observation: On 2026-07-19 with winml 0.2.0, ONNX Runtime 1.24.5, and main commit e7509b1e908c74beff0a5655b8f8d7de69c5afae, `winml inspect` for google-bert/bert-base-cased and bert-base-cased was semantically equal after ignoring identity-only paths, and explicit fill-mask CPU fp32 `winml config` output was semantically equal. The canonical recipes are examples/recipes/google-bert_bert-base-cased/cpu/cpu/fill-mask_fp32_config.json and fill-mask_fp16_config.json.

validated_on: google-bert/bert-base-cased and bert-base-cased alias @ fp32 config @ CPUExecutionProvider/cpu

gotchas: Use the canonical google-bert/bert-base-cased identity in checked-in recipe metadata even though the short alias resolves equivalently.
findings.mechanism_notes: Resolution equivalence was measured at inspect/config surfaces; the alias registration path was not independently traced to source in this learner pass.

findings.title: bert-base-cased is recipe-only coverage because current main already supports recipe-free fill-mask export
findings.observation: On 2026-07-19 with winml 0.2.0, ONNX Runtime 1.24.5, and main commit e7509b1e908c74beff0a5655b8f8d7de69c5afae, google-bert/bert-base-cased built recipe-free as BertForMaskedLM. The fp32 recipe examples/recipes/google-bert_bert-base-cased/cpu/cpu/fill-mask_fp32_config.json is semantically identical to default `winml config`; the fp16 recipe differs only by the generated `/quant` precision block. Both built on CPU without source changes. Materialized build config retained loader task fill-mask, model class AutoModelForMaskedLM, model type bert, opset 17, 1x512 int32 inputs, logits output, and `optim.clamp_constant_values=true`.

not_yet_tested_on: google-bert/bert-base-cased runtime builds on non-CPU EP/device targets

gotchas: Do not add BERT source support for this checkpoint: current main already resolves and exports it; these recipes record exact CPU precision coverage.
The fp16 recipe's generated quant block is a precision declaration, not a checkpoint-specific source repair.
findings.mechanism_notes: Recipe-free build, generated-config comparison, materialized build config, and both recipe builds directly confirmed the existing loader/export path and recipe-only delta.

findings.title: The generated CPU fp16 recipe produces a true half-precision BERT artifact while preserving float I/O
findings.observation: For google-bert/bert-base-cased on 2026-07-19 with winml 0.2.0, ONNX Runtime 1.24.5, and examples/recipes/google-bert_bert-base-cased/cpu/cpu/fill-mask_fp16_config.json, all 208 floating initializers were FLOAT16, the 5 non-floating initializers remained INT64, and external data was 261,219,464 bytes versus 522,438,928 bytes for fp32 (ratio 0.5). The quant block used mode fp16 with `fp16_keep_io_types=true`, so logits remained FLOAT.
gotchas: Do not infer fp16 from the requested precision flag alone; verify initializer dtypes and external-data size.
Float logits are expected because the generated recipe keeps I/O types.
findings.mechanism_notes: The materialized fp16 build config and ONNX initializer census directly confirm conversion and preserved float I/O.

findings.title: CPU fp16 was slower and used more RSS than fp32 for fixed 1x512 semantic BERT inputs
findings.observation: On the tested host on 2026-07-19 with winml 0.2.0 and ONNX Runtime 1.24.5, 100 measured iterations after 10 warmups on CPUExecutionProvider used fixed semantic 1x512 inputs. fp32 measured mean 249.537 ms, p50 245.162 ms, 4.01 samples/s, and 599.87 MB total RSS delta; fp16 measured mean 295.078 ms, p50 290.010 ms, 3.39 samples/s, and 648.20 MB total RSS delta. Recipes were examples/recipes/google-bert_bert-base-cased/cpu/cpu/fill-mask_fp32_config.json and fill-mask_fp16_config.json.

not_yet_tested_on: other CPU models, thread settings, sequence lengths, and hosts

gotchas: Do not assume a true fp16 artifact improves CPU latency or memory; measure both precision tuples with the same semantic inputs.
findings.mechanism_notes: The performance difference is measured on one host; no kernel-level cause was established.

findings.title: Both CPU precisions preserve masked-token rankings against PyTorch on the tested prompts
findings.observation: A self-contained named-output L2 harness on 2026-07-19 compared PyTorch logits with CPUExecutionProvider ONNX logits for three masked-token prompts. Using the fp32 and fp16 recipes under examples/recipes/google-bert_bert-base-cased/cpu/cpu, both precisions matched top-1 and all five top-5 tokens for every masked position (minimum top-5 overlap 5). fp32 full-logit cosine was 0.9999999999953111 with max absolute error 0.0000970364; fp16 cosine was 0.9999996630878892 with max absolute error 0.0882721. Environment: winml 0.2.0, ONNX Runtime 1.24.5.
gotchas: Compare the named `logits` output and masked-position rankings; full-tensor cosine alone can hide task-visible rank changes.
findings.mechanism_notes: Parity is directly measured for three prompts, but it is not a proof over all inputs.

The CPU fp32 recipe produced pseudo-perplexity 5.2357 and NLL 1.6555 in 131.536 s; fp16 produced pseudo-perplexity 5.2356 and NLL 1.6555 in 151.398 s.

findings.title: BERT static analysis records are complete across 11 EP/device targets but are not runtime support proof
findings.observation: Static analysis of google-bert/bert-base-cased fp32 and fp16 on 2026-07-19 used public rules v0.2.0 (SHA-256 6dcabbe7f5493fbc2bd23de195ab6e35b3578d510f18c2e220bc5538a1f232cc) with winml 0.2.0 and ONNX Runtime 1.24.5. Both artifacts emitted all 11 records: NvTensorRTRTXExecutionProvider/GPU, CUDAExecutionProvider/GPU, MIGraphXExecutionProvider/GPU, QNNExecutionProvider/NPU, QNNExecutionProvider/GPU, OpenVINOExecutionProvider/NPU, OpenVINOExecutionProvider/GPU, OpenVINOExecutionProvider/CPU, DmlExecutionProvider/GPU, CPUExecutionProvider/CPU, and VitisAIExecutionProvider/NPU. fp32 had 442 operators and fp16 had 443, each with 15 unique types; the preserved top three counts for both were Add=125, MatMul=98, Mul=50. All nodes mapped (442/442 fp32; 443/443 fp16). Exit 1 means partial/unsupported static coverage, not a failed scan: QNN NPU/GPU marked Div, Erf, Add, and Mul partial. OpenVINO plugin registration also logged missing onnxruntime_providers_shared.dll Error 126, while static records remained complete. The host actually exposed only DmlExecutionProvider and CPUExecutionProvider, so rule classifications and `runtime_support` fields for other targets must not be reported as executed runtime support.

validated_on: google-bert/bert-base-cased @ fp32 static analyze @ 11 named EP/device records
google-bert/bert-base-cased @ fp16 static analyze @ 11 named EP/device records

gotchas: Preserve all 11 EP/device records and the top-three counts when summarizing; do not collapse the scan to only actionable QNN rows.
Treat all-unknown or rule-derived classifications as static evidence, not as proof that a provider ran on this host.
An analyze exit code of 1 can coexist with complete JSON when the static rules classify partial or unsupported coverage.
findings.mechanism_notes: The scan completeness and classifications are confirmed, but non-CPU runtime support was not exercised and the OpenVINO DLL registration failure was not repaired in this CPU-scoped contribution.

findings.title: bert-base-cased HTP metadata records the exact traced module scale and hierarchy
findings.observation: Frozen tester fp32 and fp16 export_htp_metadata.json artifacts for google-bert/bert-base-cased on 2026-07-19, produced with winml 0.2.0 and ONNX Runtime 1.24.5 from examples/recipes/google-bert_bert-base-cased/cpu/cpu/fill-mask_<precision>_config.json, both record exactly 108,340,804 parameters and 92 traced modules out of 233. Their verified hierarchy is rooted at BertForMaskedLM with exactly two direct children: BertModel and BertOnlyMLMHead. BertModel has exactly two direct children, BertEmbeddings and BertEncoder; BertEncoder has exactly 12 direct children named BertLayer.0 through BertLayer.11, and each BertLayer has exactly three direct children named BertAttention, BertIntermediate, and BertOutput. BertOnlyMLMHead has exactly one direct child, BertLMPredictionHead, which has exactly one direct child, BertPredictionHeadTransform. This HTP hierarchy agrees with the frozen model-breakdown profile's collapsed 12-layer encoder and masked-LM-head tree. The frozen tester HTP artifact SHA-256 values are 2699d1f42f19fb5dba7953d43ccf055f86b06f343d3d0c07f1e1d5377026a2ec for fp32 and 3f79bab3a87628ad4ba0920b795b9c8ba097e9e3b1de297bd2f5af01edb075ec for fp16.

validated_on: google-bert/bert-base-cased @ fp32 @ CPUExecutionProvider/cpu @ frozen tester export_htp_metadata.json
google-bert/bert-base-cased @ fp16 @ CPUExecutionProvider/cpu @ frozen tester export_htp_metadata.json

findings.title: BertModel feature-extraction is Optimum VENDOR-ONLY, but baseline quantization can fail when the tokenizer omits token_type_ids
findings.observation: intfloat/multilingual-e5-small: config model_type=bert, architectures=[BertModel] (encoder-only, hidden_size=384, 12 layers, 12 heads, vocab_size=250037, max_position_embeddings=512, type_vocab_size=2 so it HAS token_type_ids). The Optimum-coverage probe shows bert feature-extraction / sentence-similarity fully VENDOR-ONLY (added_by_winml=[]), so no src/winml/modelkit/models/hf/bert.py change is needed -> Effort L0*. HOWEVER the baseline auto-config build `winml build -m intfloat/multilingual-e5-small` (no -c) on origin/main d9feefff FAILS: Export (61.2s, 448.3MB) and Optimize (31.1s) succeed, then Quantize crashes with `ValueError: Required inputs (['token_type_ids']) are missing from input feed (['input_ids', 'attention_mask'])` — the static-quant calibration data reader only supplies input_ids+attention_mask. The curated CPU convention recipe (quant:null, fp32+fp16 under cpu/cpu/) skips the broken quantize pass and builds a working float model in 109.4s (Export 50.5 + Optimize 58.0). So this is a genuine baseline-FAILS -> recipe-FIXES delta, not a catalog clone. Recipe shape: 3 int32 inputs input_ids[1,512] (range 0..250037) + attention_mask[1,512] + token_type_ids[1,512] (both range 0..2), output last_hidden_state[1,512,384], optim.clamp_constant_values=true, model_class=AutoModel, model_type=bert. L1 CPU perf avg 256.26ms / 3.90 samples-s / RAM +186.9MB. L2 PyTorch-vs-ONNX: raw last_hidden_state max-abs 1.729e-06, E5 mean-pooled+L2-normalized sentence-embedding cosine 1.000000, and query->passage retrieval ranking identical between PyTorch and ONNX. analyze: 384 ops, 15 unique, all supported on the analyzed EP.

not_yet_tested_on: a rebuilt CPU fp16 tuple with explicit `--precision fp16` and FLOAT16/size/perf proof
GPU/DML/QNN runtime execution for this checkpoint
whether a w8a16 recipe can be made to quantize by supplying token_type_ids to the calibration reader

gotchas: DEFAULT `winml build` (no recipe) FAILS at quantize for bert models WHOSE TOKENIZER DOES NOT EMIT token_type_ids (e.g. E5's XLMRobertaTokenizer): the calibration reader tokenizes text and feeds only what the tokenizer returns (input_ids+attention_mask), so the required token_type_ids input is missing. REFINED by bert-010: models with a classic WordPiece BertTokenizer (which DOES emit token_type_ids) quantize fine at baseline (emit w8a16) — the crash is tokenizer-dependent, not implied by type_vocab_size=2. A float recipe may bypass this quantization failure, but each requested precision still needs current recipe metadata and exact artifact proof.

E5 uses XLMRobertaTokenizer (vocab 250037) which does NOT emit token_type_ids, yet config model_type=bert (type_vocab_size=2) so the exported ONNX REQUIRES a token_type_ids input. Feed zeros (the single-segment BERT default) at inference.

E5 embeddings require 'query: ' / 'passage: ' text prefixes and mean-pooling + L2 normalization for meaningful similarity — a downstream usage detail, does NOT change the exported graph (raw last_hidden_state) or affect PyTorch-vs-ONNX parity.

The historical CPU run did not materialize the fp16 tuple. Under current `_meta-065/_meta-077`, build it with `--precision fp16` without `--no-quant` and require FLOAT16/size/perf proof; byte-identical recipe bodies do not make an fp32 artifact an fp16 PASS.
findings.mechanism_notes: Confirmed by VENDOR-ONLY Optimum probe, the reproduced baseline quantize ValueError, and the historical fp32 float-recipe build. Falsify with a bert checkpoint whose baseline build fails at EXPORT (would need per-arch code), or whose default quant calibration already supplies token_type_ids.

findings.title: BertModel embedder with a classic WordPiece tokenizer quantizes at baseline; float recipes document coverage rather than fix a crash
findings.observation: dell-research-harvard/lt-un-data-fine-fine-es: config model_type=bert, architectures=[BertModel], based on the Spanish BETO embedder hiiamsid/sentence_similarity_spanish_es (hidden_size=768, 12 layers, 12 heads, vocab_size=31002, max_position_embeddings=512, type_vocab_size=2 so it HAS token_type_ids, pad_token_id=1). Unlike bert-009 (E5), its tokenizer is a classic WordPiece BertTokenizer ([CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD]/[MASK]) which DOES emit token_type_ids, so the DEFAULT auto-config build `winml build -m dell-research-harvard/lt-un-data-fine-fine-es` (no -c) on origin/main d9feefff SUCCEEDS end-to-end: Export 35.3s + Optimize 23.3s + Quantize 45.6s -> model.onnx (127.8MB w8a16 uint8/uint16), Build complete 121.5s. So this is NOT a baseline-fails case — it FALSIFIES the generalization in bert-009 that 'the default build fails at quantize on token_type_ids models'; the failure there was driven by the XLMRobertaTokenizer not emitting token_type_ids, not by type_vocab_size=2. The recipe is still the right deliverable because the CPU convention (_meta-065) ships fp32+fp16 FLOAT, not the default w8a16. Curated recipe (quant:null, fp32+fp16 under cpu/cpu/) builds cleanly: FE 100.0s (Export 52.4 + Optimize 46.7), SS 92.3s (Export 47.1 + Optimize 44.4). Recipe shape: 3 int32 inputs input_ids[1,512] (range 0..31002) + attention_mask[1,512] + token_type_ids[1,512] (both range 0..2), output last_hidden_state[1,512,768], optim.clamp_constant_values=true, model_class=AutoModel, model_type=bert. L1 CPU perf avg 623.22ms / p50 609.55ms / min 444.80ms (bs=1, 512 tok; ~2.4x E5's 256ms because hidden 768 vs 384). L2 PyTorch-vs-ONNX: raw last_hidden_state max-abs 5.860e-04, mean-pooled+L2-normalized sentence-embedding cosine 1.000000 (min=mean), and retrieval ranking identical between PyTorch and ONNX AND semantically correct (paraphrase pair and QA pair rank at top). analyze: 384 ops, 15 unique, all supported on the analyzed EP.

not_yet_tested_on: GPU/DML/QNN runtime execution for this checkpoint
the default w8a16 baseline model's numeric quality vs PyTorch (not measured — we ship float instead)

gotchas: Do NOT assume a bert model with token_type_ids will fail the baseline quantize (bert-009) — that only happens when the TOKENIZER omits token_type_ids (XLMRoberta). A WordPiece BertTokenizer emits them and the baseline builds a w8a16 model fine. Verify by actually running the baseline build.
The recipe's job here is coverage, not crash-avoidance: baseline emits w8a16. State this honestly in the PR rather than presenting the float recipes as a baseline fix.

lt-un-data-fine-fine-es is a Spanish (BETO) embedder; pad_token_id=1 (vs E5's 0). Historical feature-extraction and sentence-similarity float recipe bodies differed only in loader.task. Current fp16 artifact proof is recorded in bert-011.

L2 max-abs diff (5.86e-04) is ~340x larger than E5's (1.73e-06) yet still << 1e-3 and cosine is 1.000000 — larger hidden (768) + clamp_constant_values accumulates more float rounding; judge parity by cosine/ranking, not raw max-abs alone.
findings.mechanism_notes: Confirmed by the successful baseline w8a16 build, historical float builds, and L2 parity. The tokenizer-dependence of the bert-009 crash is a two-point contrast: E5/XLMRoberta (no token_type_ids -> baseline quantize crash) vs lt-un-data/WordPiece-Bert (emits token_type_ids -> baseline quantize OK). The historical fp16 gap is resolved by the independent current artifact evidence in bert-011.

findings.title: Explicit fp16 selection produces a true half-size BERT artifact for both embedding tasks
findings.observation: On 2026-08-13 at winml-cli candidate 86821d476bcfcc487dc993783557e49b0a930dfb with ONNX Runtime 1.24.5, all four CPU recipe builds passed from examples/recipes/dell-research-harvard_lt-un-data-fine-fine-es/cpu/cpu/<task>_<precision>_config.json using explicit `-p fp32` or `-p fp16`. Both fp32 task artifacts were byte-identical (model SHA-256 9d132ba4ce07c483077116fce62c20cea14545a2f4151459a765e669d652e930), with 200 FLOAT initializers and 437,045,248 external-data bytes. Both fp16 task artifacts were byte-identical (model SHA-256 ffb1462d4316cf17cfe6d18b2afa85e8f0da276709795a3b19f34cf236b27d5b), with 200 FLOAT16 initializers and 218,524,672 external-data bytes, exactly half the floating-data size. All four retained three INT32 1x512 inputs and FLOAT last_hidden_state[1,512,768] output and passed real named-input inference.

not_yet_tested_on: other BERT checkpoints and non-CPU EP/device targets

gotchas: The fp32/fp16 recipe bodies intentionally keep quant:null; explicit `-p fp16` materializes the fp16 quant block, so filenames and recipe bodies alone are not precision proof.
FLOAT output is expected for fp16 because the resolved configuration sets fp16_keep_io_types=true.
findings.mechanism_notes: Initializer dtypes, external-data bytes, model hashes, and runtime output dtypes independently confirm precision realization and task-level graph identity.

findings.title: The refreshed BERT export traces three root children and a stable 12-layer hierarchy
findings.observation: All four export_htp_metadata.json artifacts produced by HTPExporter from examples/recipes/dell-research-harvard_lt-un-data-fine-fine-es/cpu/cpu/<task>_<precision>_config.json on 2026-08-13 at candidate 86821d476bcfcc487dc993783557e49b0a930dfb record BertModel with 109,850,880 parameters, 228 total modules, 88 traced modules, and 176 execution steps. The root has exactly three direct children: BertEmbeddings at execution_order 1, BertEncoder at execution_order 2, and BertPooler at execution_order 87. BertEncoder contains BertLayer.0 through BertLayer.11, and each traced layer contains BertAttention, BertIntermediate, and BertOutput. Attention further records BertSelfAttention and BertSelfOutput, while each intermediate records GELUActivation. The task-level masked mean pool remains outside the exported graph.

findings.title: Build materialization adds BERT fusion defaults and derives fp16 conversion from the precision flag
findings.observation: The four materialized winml_build_config.json files for examples/recipes/dell-research-harvard_lt-un-data-fine-fine-es/cpu/cpu/<task>_<precision>_config.json at candidate 86821d476bcfcc487dc993783557e49b0a930dfb preserve AutoModel, model_type=bert, the task-specific loader task, eager Transformers attention, opset 17, three INT32 1x512 inputs, and last_hidden_state output. Materialization expands optim to clamp_constant_values=true, gelu_fusion=true, and matmul_add_fusion=true. fp32 retains quant=null; explicit `-p fp16` derives quant.mode=fp16, fp16_keep_io_types=true, task/model metadata, and no nodes_to_exclude. findings.title: Single-segment BERT inference can synthesize a missing declared token_type_ids input without weakening strict input validation
findings.observation: On microsoft/winml-cli candidate 8e7c621a2312a3ef45b08c43e7347301e992f842 with winml 0.2.0 and ONNX Runtime 1.24.5, intfloat/multilingual-e5-small's tokenizer emitted only input_ids and attention_mask while each final CPU graph declared token_type_ids int32 [1,512]. The shared WinMLModelForFeatureExtraction.forward repair synthesized all-zero int32 [1,512] token_type_ids for feature-extraction and sentence-similarity at fp32 and fp16. Independent compatibility tests also preserved tokenizer-provided nonzero segment IDs, refused incompatible static token_type_ids shapes, and left unrelated missing required inputs to strict session validation. findings.title: multilingual-e5-small has complete static rule-backed classifications with QNN Gather partial and Where unknown
findings.observation: For all four candidate artifacts at 8e7c621a2312a3ef45b08c43e7347301e992f842, static Analyze used 24 explicit commands (4 artifacts x 6 targets) and mapped every node to a model component. Both fp32 artifacts had 372 operators and both fp16 artifacts had 373; each had 15 unique types with dominant counts Reshape=121, Gemm=72, Transpose=48, Add=38, and LayerNormalization=25. Complete rule-backed targets were NvTensorRTRTX/GPU, OpenVINO/CPU, OpenVINO/GPU, OpenVINO/NPU, QNN/GPU, and QNN/NPU. QNN GPU and NPU classified Gather partial; Where remained unknown across all six rule-backed targets. CPU, CUDA, MIGraphX, and DML rule-less groups remained all-unknown and are not runtime incompatibility proof. Evidence: temp/pr1182-tester-retry2-8e7c621a/analysis-summary.json plus 24 referenced analysis JSON files under manifest SHA-256 6badeb9464d66d0ad12a3211fc911534aab40b26481f46e99763c03f194a0bb8.
